purpose: Stage-2 PILOT: a 24-cell paired claim-validation run on a derived 6-claim subset, executed on two opencode models. Answers whether the corrected instrument produces differentiated output at all, and whether two independent models agree; it is NOT powered for a per-category rate and must never be reported as one.

harness.system_prompt: You are exploring an unfamiliar code checkout to answer a question about where specific behaviour lives. Ground every claim in a concrete file and location you found in THIS checkout; do not answer from prior memory of any upstream project. Conclude with the answer the question asks for.
harness.claim_answer_instruction: Return one JSON object {verdict: true|false|unsupported, evidence: [{path, line}], rationale}; cite only files in the checkout.

scorer.primary_metric: verdict accuracy and grounded-verdict accuracy vs the independent, forged-coordinate oracle; citation precision/recall/F1
scorer.judge: none (no LLM judge; deterministic verdict + evidence-anchor scoring)

subject_binary.name: lci
subject_binary.invocation: lci mcp (stdio), registered as server 'lci' via --mcp-config

treatment.description: LCI MCP semantic-navigation tools + Read; answers structured claims

baseline.description: Lexical Grep + Glob + Read only; no LCI server attached

task_subset.rule: one claim per author category, two per corpus, seed-7 shuffle with id tie-breaks
task_subset.note: Derived, not chosen: a hand-picked subset would let the selector choose the result. Re-drawing requires changing a committed rule and its test.

models.note: Model is arm-shared WITHIN each pair, so each model is its own complete paired experiment and the tool surface stays the only manipulated variable across arms. Running two is a robustness check on the instrument, not a model contest, and satisfies the one-real-cell-per-model-tier rule before any rate is published.
models.id_probe: `opencode models` 2026-09-22 lists both ids verbatim under opencode-go; an unserved id yields a zero-event stream, not an error, so the probe is recorded.
models.routes_note: deepseek-v4.1-flash runs on the cline-pass account at the owner's direction. qwen3.8-flash stays on opencode-go because cline-pass does not serve it (`opencode models cline-pass`, 2026-09-22, lists qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus and qwen3.8-max only). The account was tested as a cause of cell failures and ruled out: cells failed the same way on both accounts.

repetitions.note: reps=1 matches stage 1/2. With n=1 per (claim, arm, model) no spread exists, so no lift rule may be applied to this pilot -- see analysis_constraints.

budget.cells_formula: 6 claims x 2 arms x 2 models x 1 rep
budget.estimate_basis: Measured, not guessed: mean per-cell tokens over the 160 executed discovery cells in results/discovery/ (input 33542, output 918, cache_read 135791, cache_write 4168) priced at the models.dev opencode-go rates of 2026-09-22. deepseek-v4.1-flash $0.0719/12 cells, qwen3.8-flash $0.1016/12 cells. The reference class is discovery questions on other models, disclosed as inherited.
budget.ceiling_note: The ceiling is a hard stop roughly 12x the estimate, not a forecast. It was set by the harness, not named by the approver.

approval.granted_scope: Run the 12-cell pilot on opencode-go deepseek-v4.1-flash and qwen3.8-flash (both, hence 24 cells), after fixing the instrument defects.

arm_disjointness.evidence: Both arms' opencode tools maps deny every native tool the arm does not grant; neither arm is a superset of the other. For THIS runner the disjointness is re-established in exploration/runner/adapter.py and asserted both directions in tests/test_opencode_adapter.py::ArmDisjointnessTest, and the runner's gate independently re-checks every emitted call.

unfiltered_grep_baseline.reasoning: The finding is tool-level: raw grep scored recall 1.0 with precision 0.05-0.56, so an LCI win measured a filtering step the baseline never received. This pilot is AGENT-level -- the baseline arm is an agent holding Grep/Glob/Read that performs its own filtering before answering, so both arms are handed the same class of post-processing. Recorded rather than assumed, so a reader can dispute it.

analysis_constraints: No lift, effect size or significance claim: n=1 per cell yields no spread, and a degenerate spread manufactures exceptions (see the minimum-successes gate).
No per-category rate: one claim per category cannot support one.
Report per-model results separately AND their agreement; disagreement between the two models is a finding about the instrument, not a model ranking.
A provider failure is a named non-result (provider_error / provider_timeout / provider_quota / malformed_provider_stream / exit_N), never a wrong answer.
A tool-isolation violation is a rejected cell, never a scored answer.

Report answer_envelope counts per arm and per model, and report every headline number twice: all envelopes, and bare only. A difference between the two is a formatting effect, not a comprehension effect.
next.js cells are blocked by an absolute symlink in the forged corpus (task 01M34T6RMY39ABDFZEHKH87448) and are reported as config_error non-results. The subset is not re-drawn.

execution.provider_spend_note: Not measured: records kept input and output tokens only and dropped cache reads (fixed in c6f36e4 for later runs). Pre-registered estimate $0.17.
